findings.title: getCredential ignores custom UserStorageProvider credentials that only implement getCredentials
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` only queries `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and `user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`. `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` only returns credentials stored in Keycloak's `UserFederatedStorageProvider`, whereas `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)` queries both local storage and `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials(...)` (in `UserCredentialManager`). Calling `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` first and falling back to `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` (or vice versa) works here only because `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream` is also called, yet in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` the returned `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` has no `id` set (`createFromValues` does not set an ID). If all codes are used on a federated/storage credential, `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` with a `null` ID (or a storage credential ID that only `removeStoredCredentialById` handles when `id != null`), failing to remove or disable the exhausted recovery codes in user storage.

findings.title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage is meant to stay compatible with Keycloak 4.8.3 APIs
findings.body: The class-level Javadoc of `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` states: "UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3. It is used for backwards compatibility testing. Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider." Modifying this provider to use newly introduced APIs (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, `getCredentials`, Java 10 `var`) defeats the purpose of this test provider as a 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility fixture.
